articles.title: Forced Psychiatry: Courts Are Stripping Mentally Ill Patients of the Right to Refuse Treatment
articles.summary: A Reason investigation exposes the legal mechanisms allowing governments to forcibly medicate individuals diagnosed with mental illness, overriding informed consent entirely. The piece cuts to the heart of psychiatric overreach — where diagnosis becomes a weapon to nullify bodily autonomy. Patients stripped of refusal rights have no recourse against treatments with documented harms including tardive dyskinesia, metabolic syndrome, and cognitive decline.

articles.title: Estrogen Dominance, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Hormonal Framework Mainstream Medicine Refuses to Teach
articles.summary: Georgi Dinkov lays out a metabolic and hormonal framework — rooted in decades of research by Ray Peat — that directly contradicts the pharmaceutical industry's profitable models of hormonal and serotonergic disease. The piece explains how estrogen dominance is routinely misdiagnosed because standard blood panels are structurally inadequate, leaving millions undertreated or mistreated. This is exactly the kind of systems-biology thinking that gets researchers blacklisted from NIH grant pipelines.

articles.title: Mitochondria, Chronic Inflammation, and Cancer: The Metabolic Theory That Oncology Doesn't Want You to Understand
articles.summary: New research synthesis confirms what metabolic scientists like Thomas Seyfried have argued for years: mitochondrial dysfunction is a root driver of chronic inflammation and cancer risk, not a downstream consequence. This framing is systematically sidelined by an oncology establishment built on patentable chemotherapy and immunotherapy protocols that target symptoms, not causes. The research demands a rethinking of the entire cancer-as-genetic-mutation paradigm that has swallowed billions in NIH funding.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Breaks Silence on Holmes Documentary — Says It Sanitizes a Systemic Fraud
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the whistleblower who risked everything to expose Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos, is now pushing back on a new documentary he says renders Holmes 'almost unrecognizable' — softening a fraud that endangered patient lives with false diagnostic results. Shultz's critique cuts deeper than the film: regulators, investors, and media cheerleaders all failed to act on early warnings, making Theranos a case study in how institutional capture protects fraudsters until it's too late. The real story isn't Holmes in prison — it's the broken oversight system that let her operate for years.

articles.title: Martin Shkreli Defies Lifetime Pharma Ban — FTC and Seven States Demand Contempt Finding
articles.summary: The FTC and a coalition of seven states allege Martin Shkreli secretly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies in direct violation of a court-ordered lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry. The contempt motion reveals that pharma industry bans, even those handed down as landmark punishments, are effectively unenforceable against well-connected insiders with the resources to obscure their market activity. If Shkreli can do this openly, the question becomes: how many others are doing it quietly?

articles.title: Brownstone Institute Demands COVID Accountability: The Suffering and the Dead Must Not Be Forgotten
articles.summary: Brownstone Institute's Rev. John F. Naugle issues a moral indictment of the institutions — NIH, CDC, FDA, and the academic-medical complex — whose lockdown and mandate policies caused documented mass harm that has never been formally investigated. The piece names the pattern: harm was inflicted, the data was suppressed or minimized, and no official has faced professional or legal consequences. Without accountability, the infrastructure for the next round of coercion remains fully intact.

articles.title: Brownstone: COVID Accountability Is Not Optional — It Is the Only Thing That Matters Now
articles.summary: Steven Kritz at Brownstone Institute argues that without formal accountability for the scientists, bureaucrats, and policymakers who engineered COVID mandates and suppressed dissent, every future public health crisis will be managed the same way. The piece draws a direct line between the silencing of physicians like Peter McCullough and the institutional protection of figures like Anthony Fauci who have invoked the Fifth Amendment rather than testify. Accountability is framed not as political revenge but as the minimum condition for scientific integrity to mean anything.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Securities Fraud Class Action as FTC Targets Company for Deceptive Health Claims
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health is now facing both an FTC federal complaint and a securities class action lawsuit, with plaintiffs alleging company executives misled investors about the regulatory and legal risks surrounding their direct-to-consumer health model. The FTC complaint accuses the company of deceptive practices — a pattern that mirrors the broader telehealth industry's exploitation of regulatory gray zones to push medications with limited oversight. This is what happens when pharma-adjacent companies grow fast enough to believe they're above the rules.

articles.title: Fauci's Darkest Hours Exposed: What the Record Finally Shows
articles.summary: Jeffrey Tucker at Brownstone Institute dissects Anthony Fauci's most damaging decisions during the COVID era, laying out a documented case for institutional betrayal at the highest levels of American public health. The piece names the policies, the lies of omission, and the human cost of Fauci's unchecked authority. This is the accounting the corporate press refused to run.

articles.title: The Vaccinated Human Body: What They Never Modeled and Never Disclosed
articles.summary: Brownstone Institute publishes a deep examination of what post-vaccination physiology actually looks like — raising questions the FDA's approval process never seriously asked. The piece challenges the regulatory assumption that mRNA intervention effects are transient and localized. The data gap between what was studied and what was authorized is the scandal.

articles.title: Remember the Dead: COVID Policy Killed People and Nobody Is Accountable
articles.summary: Rev. John Naugle at Brownstone Institute demands a moral reckoning for the victims of lockdowns, hospital protocols, and denied treatments — deaths that official narratives continue to obscure. The piece is a direct indictment of public health administrators who prioritized institutional protection over patient lives. Accountability has been systematically avoided.

articles.title: Estrogen, Histamine, and Endotoxin: The Hormonal Theory They Don't Teach in Med School
articles.summary: Georgi Dinkov lays out a metabolic framework connecting estrogen dominance, histamine overload, serotonin dysregulation, and endotoxin burden — a model with significant explanatory power for chronic disease that mainstream endocrinology ignores. Standard blood panels miss the real picture, leaving patients misdiagnosed and undertreated. This is the alternative metabolic research that never gets NIH grant money.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Cancer: The Metabolic Theory the Oncology Establishment Buries
articles.summary: Research linking chronic inflammation and mitochondrial failure to cancer risk is presented in stark terms that challenge the dominant somatic mutation theory underpinning most oncology funding. The evidence for metabolic origins of cancer has existed for decades and has been systematically defunded and marginalized. If this framework is right, the entire chemotherapy-first paradigm deserves a hard second look.

articles.title: Mental Illness Label Does Not Erase the Right to Refuse Treatment — Courts Are Finally Saying So
articles.summary: Reason magazine confronts the legal and ethical abyss of forced psychiatric treatment, asking whether a diagnosis strips a patient of bodily autonomy — and finding the answer increasingly contested in court. Psychiatric overdiagnosis combined with state-mandated medication represents one of the least scrutinized areas of medical coercion. The piece exposes the machinery that converts dissent and distress into compliance.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Breaks Silence on Holmes Documentary: The Fraud Was Worse Than Film Shows
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the Theranos insider who risked everything to expose Elizabeth Holmes's fraudulent blood-testing empire, says the new documentary still doesn't capture the full scope of the deception. Shultz's original disclosures were met with legal intimidation and character assassination — a blueprint the medical-industrial complex uses against all whistleblowers. The Theranos case remains the clearest modern proof that investor hype and regulatory capture can kill patients.

articles.title: Martin Shkreli Defies Pharma Ban: FTC and Seven States Move for Contempt
articles.summary: The FTC and a coalition of state attorneys general allege that Martin Shkreli — already barred for life from the pharmaceutical industry — covertly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies in brazen defiance of a court order. The contempt motion exposes how even hard-won enforcement actions against pharma predators get circumvented through financial shell games. Shkreli became the face of pharma greed, but the system that enabled him has never faced equivalent accountability.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Speaks: The System That Enabled Holmes Is Still Running
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, who risked everything to expose Theranos fraud, is back in the news as a new documentary whitewashes Elizabeth Holmes. Shultz's original whistleblowing revealed how investors, regulators, and media failed catastrophically to catch years of deadly diagnostic fraud. The structural conditions that allowed Theranos to operate unchecked — regulatory capture, media capture, VC hype over patient safety — remain entirely unreformed.

articles.title: Pharma Bro Shkreli Allegedly Trading Drug Stocks Under a Lifetime Ban — FTC and Seven States Want Him in Contempt
articles.summary: Martin Shkreli, banned for life from the pharmaceutical industry, allegedly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies in direct violation of federal court orders. The FTC and seven state attorneys general are now seeking contempt sanctions and forfeiture of profits. This case exposes how pharma insiders treat regulatory penalties as minor inconveniences rather than meaningful deterrents.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Safety Failures on Its iLet Device — Stock Cratered 37% When Truth Emerged
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors and patients about the safety, efficacy, and commercial performance of its iLet medical device, triggering a securities fraud class action after shares collapsed over 37%. If the allegations hold, this is a textbook case of a medical device company burying red flags to protect its stock price at the expense of patient safety. The FDA's failure to catch or publicize these issues ahead of the crash demands scrutiny.

articles.title: Ensign Group Allegedly Manipulated Patient Safety Data While Patients Were Neglected — Now Facing Fraud Suit
articles.summary: Ensign Group, a major long-term care operator, faces securities fraud allegations after reports surfaced that it concealed patient neglect, systematic understaffing, manipulated quality metrics, and ran an illegal administrator-license rental scheme. If true, this means regulators and investors were given falsified safety data while vulnerable patients suffered the consequences. The stock dropped 8% when the truth began leaking out.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces FTC Fraud Complaint — Telehealth Giant Accused of Deceiving Patients and Investors
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, alleging the company deceived consumers and investors about its products and practices, now spawning a securities class action. This is a direct challenge to the booming direct-to-consumer telehealth model, which critics say prioritizes revenue over rigorous medical standards. Patients who trusted the platform's marketing deserve to know what was allegedly hidden from them.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: Courts Are Stripping Mental Illness Patients of the Right to Refuse Drugs
articles.summary: Reason examines the growing legal and political push to mandate psychiatric treatment for individuals deemed mentally ill, raising the question of whether a diagnosis strips a patient of bodily autonomy. Involuntary medication has a documented history of harm, overdiagnosis, and abuse — and its expansion represents a direct threat to informed consent as a foundational medical principle. The psychiatric establishment's cozy relationship with drug manufacturers who profit from expanded treatment mandates is conspicuously absent from mainstream coverage.

articles.title: IBD Study: Live Vaccines Accidentally Given to 220 Immunocompromised Patients — Zero Infections Followed
articles.summary: A study of 220 IBD patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines showed zero subsequent cases of measles, mumps, or chickenpox — directly challenging the blanket prohibition on live vaccines in this population. This finding has significant implications for vaccine policy in immunocompromised individuals, yet it remains buried in conference proceedings rather than driving guideline reform. If blanket bans are based on precaution rather than evidence, patients may be needlessly denied protection.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Rewrite Their Own DNA to Escape Treatment — Half a Million Cells Tell the Story the Oncology Establishment Ignored
articles.summary: A sweeping analysis of nearly half a million cells from dozens of pancreatic cancer patients reveals that tumor cells are in a constant state of genetic flux, actively evolving to evade every treatment thrown at them. This challenges the static tumor model that has dominated — and failed — oncology for decades, and raises uncomfortable questions about why survival rates for pancreatic cancer have barely moved in fifty years. The metabolic and evolutionary biology communities have been raising these concerns for years while the chemotherapy-first establishment collected its grants.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Speaks: The Fraud That Nearly Killed Patients and How the System Protected Itself
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the Theranos whistleblower who risked everything to expose Elizabeth Holmes' decade-long medical fraud, says Holmes is now being repackaged as a sympathetic figure in a new documentary. Shultz's testimony remains a landmark case of what happens when regulatory capture, investor hype, and media cheerleading override basic scientific accountability. The real story isn't Holmes' redemption arc — it's how long the system let the fraud run while insiders stayed silent.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Safety Failures on Its iLet Device — Stock Collapsed 37% When Truth Emerged
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors and, critically, patients about the safety and efficacy of its iLet medical device, triggering a securities fraud class action after shares cratered more than 37%. This is the pattern: bury the safety signal, book the revenue, let patients bear the risk. When the data finally surfaces, it's lawyers — not regulators — who force accountability.

articles.title: Ensign Group Concealed Patient Neglect, Falsified Staffing Data, and Billed Feds Anyway
articles.summary: Ensign Group, one of the largest post-acute care operators in the country, faces securities fraud allegations after reports surfaced that the company systematically hid patient neglect, manipulated quality and staffing metrics, engaged in improper billing, and ran an administrator-license rental scheme. Regulators had ample opportunity to catch this — they didn't. Investors lost money; patients lost care.

articles.title: FTC Finally Moves on Shkreli — But Who's Watching the Hundreds of Pharma Executives Who Never Got Banned?
articles.summary: Martin Shkreli allegedly violated his lifetime pharma industry ban by trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies, and the FTC and seven states are now seeking contempt. Shkreli is an easy villain — but his brazen price-gouging was legal, and the structural pharma predation he embodied continues unchecked across the industry. The contempt motion is real accountability; the systemic question remains unanswered.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: Mental Illness Diagnosis Does Not Erase Your Right to Refuse
articles.summary: Reason examines the growing government appetite for compelled psychiatric treatment, asking whether a diagnosis strips a patient of the fundamental right to refuse medication. The piece surfaces a largely ignored civil liberties crisis: psychiatric coercion, often backed by pharmaceutical industry lobbying for broader treatment mandates, is expanding with minimal public debate. When the state can inject you against your will, the doctor-patient relationship is dead.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With Federal Complaint and Securities Fraud Suit — Telehealth's Wild West Has Consequences
articles.summary: The FTC filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, now followed by a securities class action, alleging the company misled consumers and investors. The telehealth boom created enormous pressure to grow fast and ask questions later — and patients seeking affordable care outside the traditional system are the ones exposed when the business model collapses. Regulatory failure at the front end always becomes litigation at the back end.
